title: Understanding Django Performance
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of understanding django performance and at least two listed subtopics.
Interpret the understanding django performance example and predict its expected result.
Choose a verification step and identify one version, security, data, or troubleshooting consideration.

content.intro: Learn understanding django performance through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding Django Performance matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines understanding django performance as part of performance, caching, and scalability. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Response time and throughput; Database and application bottlenecks; Profiling before optimizing; Identifying expensive requests; Establishing performance baselines. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Response time and throughput
items.text: Response time and throughput is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Database and application bottlenecks
items.text: Database and application bottlenecks affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Profiling before optimizing
items.text: For Profiling before optimizing, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Identifying expensive requests
items.text: Identifying expensive requests is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Establishing performance baselines
items.text: Establishing performance baselines should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Response time and throughput. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to describe understanding django performance, explain the listed topics, inspect the example, and choose an appropriate verification step. Keep the scope and version caveat visible when sharing your solution.
